summary: John's 9th-great-grandfather; of Fordham Manor and West Farms, Westchester, on record 1680-1718.
bio:
William Davenport of Fordham Manor and West Farms, Westchester, is on record 1680-1718 with wife Mary (Westchester deeds, NYGBR 51:40, 52:71, 77). Bolton says 'William Davenport and his wife Mary came from England in 1670' (speculative); Giles & Franklin think he came as a boy. A John Davenport 'of Long Neck', Westchester (deed 1682/3) is a possible father (speculative). English origin unknown; Bramhall/Bromhall Cheshire and Rev. John Davenport connections unsupported or disproven.

According to the Davenport genealogy, the family Bible gives his children as Thomas (b. 1682, d. 1759), William (b. 1683, d. 1735), Francis (b. 1685, d. 1720) and Rachel, while noting that these four may not be all his children ([R4-S1]). The Bible was given to a grandson in 1759 and its entries are copies, so it is family evidence, not a contemporary record. The book's chart then names John Davenport and his wife Mary of Long Neck near New Rochelle, said to have come to America in 1670 with four children, as William's parents. The book itself calls that first generation 'a supposition'. Its only document is a deed of 15 Jan 1682/3 in which John Davenport and Mary his wife sold land on Long Neck (NY Hist. Record vol. 45 p.112) ([R4-S1]). Note that 'came from England in 1670' is told of John and Mary in one place and of William and Mary in another (Bolton).

residences.place: Fordham Manor and West Farms, Westchester County, New York, USA

sources: Giles & Franklin, Thomas Davenport, Philipstown Pioneer 1682-1759, and his Descendants (1962): https://archive.org/details/thomasdavenportp00gile (also HathiTrust wu.89066038563: https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=wu.89066038563&view=1up&seq=395) pp. xiv-xix

[R4-S1] Giles, Thomas Davenport, Pioneer, and His Descendants: family Bible entries; family chart; deed of John Davenport and Mary, 15 Jan 1682/3 (citing NYGBR vol.45 p.112) (secondary) https://archive.org/stream/thomasdavenportp00gile/thomasdavenportp00gile_djvu.txt
openQuestions: English origin; John Davenport of Long Neck.
John Davenport of Long Neck as his father is called 'a supposition' even by the family genealogy; Westchester deeds or wills of the 1680s-1690s are needed.

events.title: Children recorded in the Davenport family Bible
events.description: The Bible, presented by Thomas Davenport (1682-1759) to his grandson Thomas on 25 Aug 1759, records that William Davenport of Fordham and his wife Mary (surname not known) had Thomas (1682-1759), William (1683-1735), Francis (1685-1720) and Rachel [R4-S1]
